text: Which genome assembly strategy represents reads as edges connecting (k-1)-mer nodes and reconstructs the sequence by finding an Eulerian path?
explanation: De Bruijn graph assembly decomposes reads into k-mers, uses (k-1)-mers as nodes and k-mers as edges, and solves the tractable, polynomial-time Eulerian path problem — the basis of tools like SPAdes and Velvet. Overlap-Layout-Consensus instead builds a graph with reads as nodes and overlaps as edges, requiring the NP-hard Hamiltonian path problem, which is why de Bruijn graphs scale better for the huge volumes of short reads.
